vid_urls.title: Progress 97 Cargo Ship Docking
vid_urls.description:
Watch the unpiloted Roscosmos Progress 97 resupply spacecraft approach the International Space Station after a two-day journey. The spacecraft will autonomously dock at 7:11 a.m. EST (1211 UTC).

For more than 25 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs that aren’t possible on Earth.

The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis program, and to Mars.

Learn more about the International Space Station, its research, and crew at: https://www.nasa.gov/station

name: ESA Hera First Images Reveal of Dimorphos

info_urls.title: Four years after NASA’s asteroid impact, ESA’s Hera reveals what happened to Dimorphos
info_urls.description: on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, 11:00 – 14:00 CET at Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, Invalidenstraße 43, 10115 Berlin, Germany and online (connection details sent to accredited media)

vid_urls.title: Revealing Hera's first images of asteroid Dimorphos
vid_urls.description:
Join us live for the Hera Mission's first images of her destination - the asteroid Dimorphos! Four years ago, humans impacted an asteroid for the very first time with @NASA's DART mission, and the European Space Agency sent the Hera mission to find out exactly what happened. 
 
This livestream, broadcast live from Berlin’s Museum für Naturkunde, will reveal Hera's first images of Dimorphos. The binary asteroid system of Didymos and its moonlet Dimorphos will be seen up-close, and the photos will reveal how DART's impact affected the 151m diameter asteroid. 
 
You'll hear from Hera’s leading scientists as they discuss whether DART and Hera have proved if asteroid deflection is a viable planetary defence method, and how the up-close look at an asteroid allows them to peek at what these ...

image.name: Hera being enclosed within its launcher fairing.

description:
ESA invites accredited journalists to an exclusive European Media Conference at the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, with participation in person and online. Leading experts will present the first detailed images of Dimorphos after NASA’s DART impact, acquired by ESA’s newly arrived Hera mission, and their initial scientific interpretation.

What happened when DART struck Dimorphos in 2022? Did the impact leave a crater, substantially reshape the asteroid, or both? Hera’s historic new images will provide the first detailed post-impact view of Dimorphos and may begin to answer questions that have remained open for four years.

The morning briefing gives journalists advance access to the imagery, the science team and interviews under embargo. Media may publish from 18:30 CET, ahead of ESA’s official public presentation of the images at ~20:00 CET during the evening ESA’s “Double Impact!” event.

From DART’s successful deflection to Hera’s historic post-impact view

In September 2022, NASA’s DART spacecraft deliberately struck Dimorphos, shortening its orbital period around Didymos by approximately 33 minutes. Yet the physical consequences of the impact remain uncertain. Hera’s investigation will help reveal how the asteroid responded and improve our ability to predict the effectiveness of kinetic-impact deflection for other asteroids.

The November images are only the beginning. Subsequent close-range investigations by Hera and its two CubeSats, Milani and Juventas, will measure the asteroids’ properties in far greater detail, including Dimorphos’ mass, surface and internal structure. Together, these data will help scientists validate models for future planetary-defence missions.

European Media Conference – 11:00 CET

Date: Wednesday, 25 November 2026

Time: 11:00 – 14:00 CET

Venue: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin, Invalidenstraße 43, 10115 Berlin

Participation: In person and online

vid_urls.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Undocking
vid_urls.description:
Watch as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft undocks from the International Space Station and begins its journey back to Earth. The uncrewed Dragon is carrying scientific research samples and hardware including a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct and frozen microbial samples.

The spacecraft will reenter Earth's atmosphere Nov. 21 and will splash down off the Californian coast at approximately 5:04 p.m. EST (2:04 p.m. PST, 2204 UTC).

Learn more about NASA's SpaceX CRS-35 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crs-35/
Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/
